title: Agent swarms
new: lyra can give one task to two to six agents at once for their separate takes. They run side by side, each with its own task on the conversation's board, and lyra gets every result to compare and combine.

title: Agents talk to each other
new: Agents can ask each other a quick question while they work and get the answer straight back.

lyra can call a huddle: two to four agents take turns discussing a question, each hearing what the others said, before lyra decides. The discussion shows as one card in the chat and is kept on the conversation's task board.

Agents start each other's work: a task one agent puts on the board for another begins as soon as the first is done, side by side with any others, and its result comes back with the first agent's ([agents] board_autostart).
improved: Every one of these keeps the usual limits: how deep hand-offs may go, how many run at once, each agent's tool budget and approvals, and a record of each exchange. Members' agents still never reach the Operator or the Coder.

title: Agents work side by side
new: When lyra hands several tasks to agents in one go, they now run side by side instead of one after another, up to three at once ([agents] max_parallel). Agents that hand work on do the same.

Each conversation has a task board shared by lyra and its agents. They can post tasks for each other, leave notes for another agent, take a task and record how it went. It shows in the chat as a Task board card, and in the terminal's Agents panel.
improved: Each agent's work keeps its own card in the chat, even when the same agent does two things at once. Every delegation still keeps its own instructions, tool budget, approvals and record.

title: How lyra compares
improved: A written comparison of lyra with Grok Bot, Meta Muse and OpenClaw is now in the docs. It says where lyra leads, where it matches them, where it's behind, what's missing entirely, and what would matter most next.

title: Notes, lists and documents told apart
new: Each card on the Notes page now says whether it's a Note, a List or a Document.
Notes started with New document, and those moved from the old Documents page, are documents. In the editor you can switch any of them between a note and a document.

title: Memories by kind
new: The Memory page can now also be filtered by kind: Semantic (facts), Episodic (events) or Working (short-term notes). Each shows how many there are, and it works together with the filter for whose memories they are (agent, user, project) and with search.

title: Notes and documents are one
improved: Notes and Documents are now one Notes page. Quick notes, lists and longer documents sit together, and any note opens in the editor, where lyra drafts or revises it and it goes to Word, OneDrive or an email draft.
A note's file follows its title: retitle it in the editor and it's renamed, without ever replacing another note.
Your existing documents were moved into your notes, so lyra's note tools and search now find them too.

title: Devices by person
improved: The Devices page now groups phones, browsers and terminals by the person they belong to, most recently used first, with machines in their own group. Each group shows how many there are and how many are online, and a long list folds after five.
fixed: A link to the Devices page (from a notification or an address) now opens it.

title: Each person's usage
new: On the Usage page, admins can choose a person's name to see their account (role, sign-in, last seen, devices), their usage day by day, by kind and by model, and the conversations that used the most.
The Usage page now lists the biggest conversations, diagnoses and routine runs in the period you choose.

title: Chats, diagnoses and routines apart
improved: The conversation list keeps your own chats by date, and puts lyra's diagnoses and routine runs in their own foldable Diagnoses and Routines sections, each with a count.
Routine runs are listed by the routine's name, and diagnoses by the problem they look into, without the bracketed prefix.
lyra only suggests folders for your own chats, not for routine runs or diagnoses.

title: A second fallback model
new: You can now set up a second fallback model ([second_fallback_model], or on the Settings page). When the chat model and the first fallback both can't be reached, it answers, and the chat says which model did.
Background jobs go to the first fallback set to take them. Your best fallback can wait for the chats while a lighter model does the small jobs.
The second fallback has its own row on the Status page and can be marked known down.

title: Status moves under System
improved: Status is now the first page in the System group on the side rail, next to Machines and Devices, instead of being a group of its own.

title: Today page; Status is for admins
new: A new Today page under Work shows your morning briefing, your end-of-day recap and what lyra is watching for you. Briefing and recap notifications now open it.
improved: The Status page now holds only lyra's own health checks, and only admins can see it. Members no longer see the Status page or get /status.

title: Tidy files and problems you can see
new: Old conversations (not pinned), uploaded files, old usage and activity logs, and phones or browsers unused for 90 days are now tidied once a day. You can change how long each is kept under [retention] in config.toml, and 0 keeps them forever. Paired machines are never removed.
The Status page has a Lyra's files row showing how many conversations, uploads, logs and devices are kept and how much space they use.

Problems that used to reach only the server log now show in Activity and on the Status page's Problems row, for the last day. These are emails that couldn't be sent, results that couldn't be kept, and files that couldn't be read and were set aside.
improved: The server's main loop was split into smaller tested parts, and the pages members may open are now one checked list. Behaviour hasn't changed, and future fixes are safer.

title: Safer saving everywhere
fixed: Two changes to the settings at once (from the Settings page, a command, lyra's own tuning) can no longer lose one of them, and config.toml keeps its private permissions.
lyra's tuned behavior, workflows, tools and agent files are saved whole or not at all, so a restart part way never leaves a half-written file.
improved: The databases now use only SQL that PostgreSQL also understands, for an easier move later.

title: Background work always knows whose it is
fixed: Every background job lyra starts (a page, a routine's check, an email, a lookup) keeps working for the person who started it. A new one can't quietly fall back to the owner's Microsoft account or PMI.
improved: lyra's tests now cover each person's routines, past results, run records, resume after a restart and email choices, in a throw-away folder that never touches real data.

title: A test for the silence limit
improved: lyra's checks now confirm a silent model gets 3 minutes before the fallback takes over.

title: Sturdier under trouble
fixed: A model that takes a request and then says nothing no longer leaves a conversation stuck. After 3 minutes of silence the fallback answers instead; if the model went quiet part way through an answer, lyra says so.
The paired devices and users lists can't be wiped by two changes at once or by a damaged file. Changes wait their turn, the last good copy is kept, and a file that won't read is never taken as empty.

Conversations stay quick while lyra looks things up: checking your calendar for quiet time, finding a saved conversation, the Usage and Past results pages, and Running now's costs no longer hold up everyone else.
A backup cut off part way (a restart, a crash) is never mistaken for a good one or used to throw away an older good one, and a restart waits for a backup in progress.
A routine that finished just before a restart keeps its result and is marked done, not interrupted, even if its check or email hadn't happened yet.

title: Groups that stay open
new: Keep rail groups open: on Profile → Layout, switch on Always open for the groups you use most, or tap the pin at the bottom of an open group. They stay unfolded while the others fold one at a time. Remembered on each device.

title: Quicker research early on
fixed: Web research keeps its early steps quick: pages are read as they are while a conversation is still small, and condensed only once it has grown (when the context starts to cost more than the summary takes).

title: Rail groups fold open
improved: The rail's groups fold open in place instead of opening a menu beside the rail. Tap Work, Knowledge, Automation, System or Help to show its pages under it; the others fold away, and the group you're working in opens by itself.

title: Quicker page summaries
fixed: Web research is quicker: page summaries are kept short (they were up to five times longer than asked, which made each step of a long routine slow), and short pages are read as they are.

title: A tidier rail
improved: The left rail shows a few groups instead of every page: Chat, Status, Work, Knowledge, Automation, System and Help. Tap one for a small menu of its pages. A group lights up while you're on one of its pages, shows that page's name, and adds up anything waiting inside it.

title: Profile and a tidier Settings
new: Profile: your own page, from the menu under your initials. Account (password, devices), Connections (Outlook, PMI), Email from lyra, this device's notifications, and Privacy.
improved: Settings is split into sections (Models, Replies, Working hours, Briefing and recap, Notifications, Email services) instead of one long page. Changes in several sections are saved together, and a • marks a section with unsaved changes.
What lyra knows about me keeps to what lyra keeps: your memories, how you write and what it did. Accounts, password, devices and email moved to your Profile.
The More page is shorter: notifications and Outlook moved to your Profile, which has its own button there.
Connecting Outlook brings you back to Profile → Connections, and lyra's hints about connecting point there too.

title: Stop at once
fixed: Stop works at once, even while the model is thinking or not answering. Before, it waited for the model's next words.

title: Routines that remember, research that's lighter
new: Routines remember: each run sees its last two results, so a daily brief builds on yesterday's instead of repeating it. You can turn this off for a routine.
Past results: every run's whole result is kept. Read and search them on the Routines page (Past results, or a routine's Results).
Each routine run shows what it took: model calls, tokens in and out, and the cost when prices are set.
Forgot your password? On the sign-in page, lyra emails a one-time link to the address on your account (it works for 30 minutes).
Running now (admins): everything lyra is working on, for everyone. It shows how long each has run, what it's doing, what it has cost so far, and a Stop button.
improved: Lighter web research: long pages are condensed to the facts, dates and links that matter by the background model before the chat model reads them, and a round's searches and page reads run side by side.
Restarting lyra waits up to 75 seconds for running routines, replies and write-ups to finish. A routine still running after that starts again by itself when lyra is back.

title: Long routines finish
fixed: A routine that reaches its tool-call limit still writes its report from what it found. Before, it stopped with nothing to email.
Routines and problem write-ups no longer pause for questions or a 5-second steps preview nobody is there to see.
Long research no longer runs out of room: when a conversation outgrows the model's context, older fetched pages are shortened (the newest stay whole).

title: Routines you can follow
fixed: A routine you start with Run now shows as Running on the Routines page: since when, what it's doing now, and a link to watch it. Its result shows when it's done.
A run cut off by a restart says so (interrupted) instead of vanishing.

Routines are run by lyra itself, not handed to a specialist agent because of words in them. A research brief that mentions "repository" no longer goes to the Coder. @machine and @all still go to the Operator.

title: Long routines fold
fixed: Long routine instructions fold to their start on the Routines page, with Show all, and their sections are spaced so they read as sections.

title: Routines in Markdown
improved: A routine's instructions show as Markdown on the Routines page: headings, lists, bold and links. They're saved exactly as you write them, line breaks and | included.
Each run's result on the Routines page shows as Markdown too.

title: Long text in dialogs
fixed: Pasting a long text into a box no longer pushes a dialog off the screen. The box scrolls once it's tall, the dialog stays inside the window (above the keyboard on phones), and its buttons stay in view.

title: More than one email service
new: Admins can add as many email services as they like in Settings → Email: Postmark, Resend or SendGrid, each with its own name, sender and key. They're tried in order, so if one fails the next sends instead. Test each one, change the order, turn one off or remove it.
About me shows which services your email goes through, in order.
improved: A setup with one email service from before carries over as the first in the list, key and all.

title: Email from lyra
new: Routines can email you their result. Set one up like "every morning at 7, search the web for news about X and summarize it with links", tick Email me each result, and lyra writes the answer as an email and sends it to you.
Get your morning briefing and end-of-day recap by email: About me → Email from lyra.
Ask "email me this" in a chat and lyra sends you a summary, a list or a write-up with links.
Emails come from lyra's own mailbox through Postmark (admins add the key and sender in Settings → Email) or, if you prefer, your own Outlook. lyra only ever emails you, never anyone else.
Admins can add an email address for people who sign in without Microsoft (Users → Add email).

title: Ask lyra what changed
new: Ask lyra about its own history: "When was password sign-in added?", "What changed lately?" or "What version is this?". It looks in What's new and answers with the version and date.

title: Search What's new
new: Search What's new: type a word or two ("calendar", "passwords", a version like 0.38) to see only the releases that mention them, ten at a time.

title: What's new in pages
improved: What's new shows ten releases at a time, with Newer and Older at the top and bottom, so it opens quickly however long the history gets.

title: A better chat
new: lyra asks for what's missing in a small form right in the chat, like who an email goes to, instead of guessing or asking in a long reply. Fill it in and it carries on.
Before lyra does several things at once, it shows the steps for a few seconds so you can skip any. Tap Skip to pause it, then Go. You can turn this off for a conversation.
Chat only: a switch in the message box turns tools off for the whole conversation, for when you just want to talk.
Edit your last message and send it again, or Retry a reply. Ask the other model (the fallback) to answer instead with one tap.
Keep going: when a reply breaks off on an error, it says what was already done, and Keep going picks up from there. Try again resends your message when nothing was done yet.
improved: The same tool failing again and again is folded into one line, like "mail_send · tried 3 times: no draft", so replies aren't buried under cards. Tap it to see them.
Steps you skip or say no to show as Denied, not as errors.
In the terminal client (lyra connect), you can answer lyra's forms and steps by typing.

title: Just chatting
new: Just chatting: a greeting, a thank-you or a "test message" gets an answer in words. lyra no longer reaches for tools on its own, so nothing is drafted, sent or changed by a guess. When you do ask it to do something, it still finds the right tool.
fixed: lyra no longer asks you to approve sending an email with no recipient or subject. A send without a real draft is turned back to lyra, which asks you what you meant.
After you say no to something, lyra doesn't ask again in the same reply. It tells you what it would have done, or asks what you'd like instead.

title: Fallback model for background jobs
new: The fallback model can take lyra's small background jobs while the main chat model is up: remembering things from your chats, skill reviews, mail triage, briefing notes, routine checks and feedback analysis. The main model is left to answer you. Turn it on in Settings (Fallback does background jobs) or with background = true under [fallback_model]. If the fallback can't do a job, the main model does it.

title: Sign in without Microsoft
new: Accounts with a username and password: admins add a person on the Users page (or /users add) and give them the one-time password shown. They choose their own when they first sign in. No Microsoft 365 account needed; they can still connect Outlook later if they have one.
Reset password on the Users page (or /users password) gives someone a new one-time password, or a username and password to someone who only had Microsoft sign-in.
Change your own password on What lyra knows about me.
improved: The sign-in page offers a username and password, Microsoft or a pairing code, whichever this server has. Repeated wrong passwords lock that username for 15 minutes.

title: Known down
new: Known down: when you already know a model is down, mark it on the Status page (open its row, add a note if you like). lyra stops trying it until you say it's back: chats go straight to the fallback model without waiting, and nobody gets "is down" alerts about it. The Status page still checks it and tells you when it answers again.

title: Fallback for agents and plans
fixed: Agents and plans use the fallback chat model too while the main one can't be reached, so a delegated job or a plan step doesn't fail when the main model is down.

title: Fallback priced right
fixed: AI usage prices replies from the fallback chat model at the fallback's own prices ([fallback_model] input_cost_per_mtok …), not the main model's.

title: A fallback chat model
new: A fallback chat model: when lyra's main model can't be reached, another one answers instead, and the chat tells you so. lyra goes back to the main model on its own once it's answering again. Admins set it on the Settings page (Models), and the Status page checks it.

title: Saved prompts on a new chat
improved: A new chat shows your saved prompts with the usual starters: tap one to put it in the message box and finish it.

title: What lyra knows about me
new: "What lyra knows about me" (in the menu under your initials): everything lyra keeps about you on one page: what it remembers (correct or forget each one), how you write, your connected accounts (disconnect any), your devices, and what it did for you. Export takes a copy of all of it.

Why? on everything lyra does: each change it made for you (a task created, an email flagged, a meeting moved, a file written) opens to what prompted it (your message, or the email mail triage looked at), the skills in play, and whether you said yes first.

title: Documents
new: Documents: write a letter, memo or one-pager with lyra. Type on one side; on the other, ask lyra to draft it or change it ("make it more formal", "shorten it") and look at its version before using it.

A finished document downloads as a Word file, saves to your OneDrive (in a "lyra" folder), or goes onto a new email draft as an attachment. Saving to OneDrive needs one more permission: if you connected Outlook before today, connect it again (More → Outlook).

title: Meetings
new: Meetings: a page for each of your meetings. Before, what to prepare (who's coming, your last emails with them, open tasks); during, a notes box that saves as you type; after, the follow-up: a summary, the decisions, your action items (each one a task with a tap) and a mail to everyone who was invited, ready in your Outlook Drafts.
When the meeting was transcribed in Teams, the follow-up is written from the transcript; otherwise from your notes.

title: Saved prompts
new: Saved prompts: the bookmark button by the message box keeps the requests you make often. Tap one to put it in the box, change it if you like, and send. Save what you've typed as a new one any time.
Admins can share prompts with everyone; lyra starts with a few: your weekly status, summarizing a thread, a reply in your style, and meeting prep.

title: Home-screen shortcuts
new: Long-press the lyra icon on your phone's home screen for New chat, Add task and Quick note: each opens straight where you need it, ready to type.

title: Smoother when it's busy
fixed: Opening Mail, Calendar, Tasks or the conversation list, searching, or pressing a button that asks Outlook or PMI no longer makes everyone else's chat wait, and a slow page no longer freezes the rest of your app.
A file attached to a message is read without holding anyone up, and a picture can no longer end up attached to your next message by mistake.
Find a time sees every meeting on a busy calendar, so it doesn't offer time you're already booked.
AI usage counts the last evening of each month.
A folder you trust on one PC no longer lets lyra change a same-named folder on another PC without asking.
Conversation folder suggestions are made once each, and never over a folder you picked yourself.
Nightly backups are much smaller: indexes lyra rebuilds on every start are left out, and the capabilities index no longer keeps every old copy of itself.

title: Every page in reach
improved: On a phone or a short laptop screen the page icons on the left are more compact, and when some don't fit, an arrow at the bottom says how many more there are (or that something is waiting there). Tap it to see them.

title: Fits your phone's screen
fixed: On a phone the app stays put: typing no longer pushes the top (and the logo) off the screen or leaves a black gap at the bottom, and the message box sits right above the keyboard.
The menu on a phone keeps clear of the status bar and the home bar, so the logo and your initials are fully visible.

title: Your folders and skills stay yours
fixed: Project folders are now kept for each person, not for the browser: on a shared PC, lyra only works in the folders of whoever is signed in. Folders added before this couldn't be told apart, so each person adds theirs again on the Projects page.
Looking up a skill's history (or rolling one back) no longer shows someone else's personal skill.

title: Replace your PMI token
fixed: The PMI connection box stays on the Tasks page once you're connected (at the bottom), so you can paste a new token to replace the old one.

title: Connect your own PMI
fixed: The Tasks page lets each person connect their own PMI account: paste an access token from PMI (Your account → Security) and press Connect. It used to send everyone to a server command that only sets the owner's.

title: Saved tokens stay saved
fixed: Saving one token (like a refreshed Microsoft sign-in) could erase the others, such as the PMI connection and Microsoft sign-in itself. Tokens are now saved one at a time and in one step, so nothing else is lost.

title: Your own briefing
fixed: Members can see their own briefing and press Brief me now, instead of being told it's for admins.
Brief me now makes only your briefing: nobody else gets one pushed because you asked.

title: Longer jobs, and Continue
new: When lyra reaches its limit of tool calls in one reply, it keeps the work done so far and offers Continue (or just say "continue") instead of ending with an error.
Admins set how many tool calls a reply may take: for everyone on the Settings page, and for one person on the Users page (or /users rounds <who> <n>), up to 64.
fixed: A reply that stopped at the tool-call limit now counts toward AI usage.

title: Works on a bad connection
new: Messages you write while offline, or while lyra is still answering, wait in the chat and are sent in order as soon as lyra can take them. You can edit or cancel one until it goes, and one sent just as the connection dropped is sent again rather than lost.
What you're typing is kept for each conversation, even if you lose the connection, reload or close the app.
The app opens with your last conversation when lyra can't be reached.

title: Settings page
new: Admins have a Settings page (in the menu under your initials, and in More): the chat model and its server and prices, the vision and decision models, your working hours and days, the morning briefing and the end-of-day recap, and what lyra pushes and does by itself. Every value is checked before it's saved, and changes apply at once without a restart.
In the terminal, /settings lists the same settings and /settings <key> <value> changes one.

title: Much faster on phones
fixed: The app is now sent compressed, so it downloads about four times faster: on a typical phone connection the first screen shows in about 2.5 seconds instead of about 10.

title: Faster to open
improved: The app opens faster, especially on phones: it loads about a third less at the start. Pages like Feedback, Q&A, Usage, Tasks and Memory load the first time you open them, and code highlighting loads with the first reply that has code.
After lyra is updated, a page opened in an app that was already open loads the new version instead of failing.

title: Clearer Microsoft 365 messages
fixed: When Microsoft 365 refuses or can't find something (a file, a chat, a mail), lyra says so plainly instead of talking about calendar events or Outlook permissions.
Teams messages that show HTML code as text (like <tag>) now read the way they were written.

title: Safer saving
fixed: A watch you added or cancelled while lyra was checking your others no longer disappears or comes back.
Stopping a watch with no name no longer stops your first one by mistake.

lyra's saved lists (watches, recaps, feedback, Q&A, routines, notes, writing style, briefings and more) are saved in one step, so a crash or two saves at once can't leave a half-written file. A file that can't be read is kept aside instead of being written over.

title: The right version everywhere
fixed: The Status page's server line, the About details and lyra's connection for coding agents show lyra's real version instead of 0.1.0.

title: Health check shows the real version
fixed: lyra's health check (/health) reports lyra's own version instead of 0.1.0.

title: Tidier inside
improved: lyra's code is reorganised so changes are quicker and safer to make. Nothing changes in how it works; settings now load the same way on start and on reload, by design.

title: Ready for a bigger database later
improved: New database work follows a rule that keeps it portable, so lyra could move to PostgreSQL later without a rewrite.

title: Status and roadmap
improved: A full overview of where lyra stands: what works, known issues, gaps, and the roadmap (status.md in the project).

title: Questions and Q&A
new: Ask a question from the Feedback page, next to bug reports and feature requests.
lyra drafts an answer from its documentation; an admin edits it and publishes it to Q&A, and you're told your question was answered (the answer is in its thread too).
A Q&A page for everyone (in the rail, above Feedback): the questions people asked and their answers, with search. Admins can add, change and remove entries.
lyra looks in Q&A when you ask it how to do something with lyra.

title: Enhance on the feedback form
new: An Enhance button under the description on the bug report and feature request form: lyra rewrites what you wrote more clearly, keeping your meaning and facts, and never adding details you didn't give.
Where something useful is missing, the draft says what to add in [brackets].
You edit the draft, then choose Use this or Keep mine; nothing changes until you do.

title: lyra reads your feedback
new: When you send a bug report or a feature request, lyra writes a short summary of how it understood it, shown with yours.
Admins also get lyra's read: the likely cause and possible fixes for a bug, a possible implementation and its size for a feature, and questions worth asking (tap one to ask it in the thread).
lyra uses its own documentation and what attached screenshots show; admins can have it read one again after replies add detail.

title: Feedback: bug reports and feature requests
new: A Feedback page (in the rail, above What's new) with two parts: send a bug report or a feature request, and follow where yours stand.
Bug reports say how bad it is, and can carry screenshots or files.
Each one moves through New, Reviewing, Planned, Done (with the version it shipped in) or Won't do, and has a comment thread with the admins.
You get a note when yours changes or someone replies; admins get one for each new submission and each of your comments. A badge shows what's new for you.
Or just tell lyra: "report a bug: …" or "I'd like lyra to …", and it files it for you.
improved: Admins see everyone's, set status and priority, and reply; members see only their own.

title: What's new where you'll find it
improved: What's new now sits at the foot of the sidebar's rail, just above your initials.

title: What's new and version numbers
new: This What's new page: every change to lyra, newest first.
lyra has a version number (major.minor.fix.build), shown in the menu under your initials.
After an update, a note tells you the new version and links here.

title: Assistant: finding times, recaps, watches and more
new: Find a time: "find 30 minutes with Dana and Juan next week" checks everyone's free/busy and suggests slots in your working hours; pick one and lyra sends the invite after your Allow.
End-of-day recap at the end of your working day: today's meetings, tasks that slipped, mail waiting and how tomorrow starts. On the Status page too, and /recap.
"Tell me when …": lyra watches for mail from someone, a reply to a thread, a PMI task changing or a Teams message, and lets you know. See and stop them on the Status page.

Meeting follow-up: after a Teams meeting, lyra summarizes the transcript, lists decisions and action items, offers your items as tasks and drafts the follow-up mail (once an admin turns transcripts on).
Search everything with Ctrl-K (⌘K): conversations, notes, memories, mail, Teams and files at once.
Read replies aloud: a speaker on each reply, an auto-read switch for the car, speed and your device's voices.
Your own skills: what lyra learns from your conversations is yours alone, and you approve, reject or stop it on the Skills page.
improved: When lyra wants to change a file in a project folder, the Allow card shows the change line by line (removed in red, added in green).

title: A richer chat
new: Pictures and scanned PDFs you attach in chat are read by the vision model, so lyra knows what they show.
Files you attach show as chips with previews and stay on your message.
Approvals appear right at the step that asks.
An agent's work is a card you can fold away, with its steps inside.
Sources under answers: the web pages used and the memories lyra recalled.
A small meter under each reply shows how much of the model's context it used, with tokens and cost on hover.
Starter prompts on an empty chat.
Plans show their steps, recovery points and Run / Cancel above the composer.
Command output looks like a terminal, folder listings like a tree, and file contents are highlighted.
Admins switch models by tapping the model name in the composer.
improved: lyra's teal (from its icon) as the accent colour.
Names under the sidebar's icons on desktop too.
A quieter New conversation button.

title: A tidier sidebar
new: Conversations grouped: Pinned, your folders, then Today, Yesterday, This week, This month, Earlier, and Archived.
Pin, move to a folder or archive a conversation from its ⋯ menu; lyra suggests a folder for new ones.
improved: lyra's pages moved to a slim icon rail, so the sidebar beside it is just your conversations, one line each.
On a phone the bottom tab bar is gone (everything is in the sidebar); a dot on the menu button means something is waiting.
Names under the icons on a phone.
fixed: The icon column no longer shows a sideways scroll bar.

title: Project folders, PDFs and pictures
new: Projects: lend lyra a folder on your own PC (Chrome or Edge); it can list, read, search and, with your Allow, write files there. Only you can reach it.
Always allow a folder, so lyra writes there without asking each time.
lyra reads PDFs, and with a vision model scanned PDFs and pictures too.
Every model's cost (embeddings, reranker, decisions, vision) counts in AI usage.
